photos.c: This photograph is part of the complete one taken at the Belgrave 50th Anniversary Dinner 1937 and shows as numbered some of the club's race walkers of that period. No 7 is Harold King (see obituary notice) others are 1. Chas Churcher, 2. Harry Churcher, 3. Joe Coleman, 4. Tommy Green, 5. Jack Bidgood and 6. Frank Elson.

The caption that goes with this photograph in our archives reads:
"Walk Match at Battersea circa 1938. Starters include H.G. Churcher, C.E.Churcher, D.E. Brown, A.A.Harley, F. Jarvis, C.W.Redgrave."
Our first stab at actually naming the faces came up with Don Brown (1), Harry Churcher (7), Charlie Churcher (23), C.W. Redgrave (24) and Alf Harley (behind Brown). However, as others have become involved and have cast their eyes over the picture, we are now not at all sure of anyone except Alf Harley. For instance, we are told that Charlie Churcher did not wear glasses and the chap next to Harry, second from the left, may be Jack Rutland If any reader can help us with more specific details of the race then we would be very pleased to hear from them.

Harry Churcher finishes 5th in the final of the 10,000m Walk at the 1948 Olympics held in London.

This photograph is part of the complete one taken at the Belgrave 50th Anniversary Dinner 1937 and shows as numbered some of the club's race walkers of that period. No 7 is Harold King (see obituary notice) others are 1. Chas Churcher, 2. Harry Churcher, 3. Joe Coleman, 4. Tommy Green, 5. Jack Bidgood and 6. Frank Elson.
Belgrave's leading walker of 1946 was Harry Churcher. He went on to take 5th place in the 10,000 metres Walk at the 1948 Wembley Olympics.

Wimbledon Common c.1950, with Len Coleman (far left) and Harry Churcher (second from right) race walking four abreast along The Causeway with not the slightest need to worry about the traffic. Photographer unknown.

The caption that goes with this photograph in our archives reads:
"Walk Match at Battersea circa 1938. Starters include H.G. Churcher, C.E.Churcher, D.E. Brown, A.A.Harley, F. Jarvis, C.W.Redgrave."
Our first stab at actually naming the faces came up with Don Brown (1), Harry Churcher (7), Charlie Churcher (23), C.W. Redgrave (24) and Alf Harley (behind Brown). However, as others have become involved and have cast their eyes over the picture, we are now not at all sure of anyone except Alf Harley. For instance, we are told that Charlie Churcher did not wear glasses and the chap next to Harry, second from the left, may be Jack Rutland If any reader can help us with more specific details of the race then we would be very pleased to hear from them.

photos.c: "I DON'T WANT TO BE A BIG STAR, but I do want to be a bloody good actor. That's why I'm behaving like a lunatic." Hence this picture. Cantering in the background is Michael Crawford (soon to be seen with Barbra Streisand in the Hollywood version of "Hello Dolly") who has just been signed to appear in Michael Winner's next film, "The Games," based on the novel by Hugh Atkinson and researcher Phillip Knightley. "The Games" recounts the trials of four Olympic marathon runners and to ensure the authenticity of the athletics in his film, Winner has hired Gordon Pirie as his technical adviser. It is Pirie (see above) who leads Crawford on training sessions across Wimbledon Common. "My training might not make much difference to audience reaction," says Crawford, "but the extra muscle will make me feel it's right." Next part: "The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner"

Pictured left: For thirteen years Leo Coy (left) has been half of the two-man management team that took the Bels. on the long road from the Southern League to the heights of the British Athletics League Division One. His partner through all that time, Bill Laws, paid tribute to Leo after the opening BAL match this year ... "He is surely one of the the sport's all-time greats when it comes to team management."
Leo intends to concentrate on our McDonalds Young Athletes' Team and we have no doubt that he will be just as successful there. Assistant GB Team Manager John Jeffery (right), who has been easing himself into our administrative ranks over the past season or two, will be taking Leo's place and helping Bill to lead our BAL team to even greater success.

photos.c:
Some interesting styles in baton changing at the 100 x 1 mile relay.
Top left. Kevin Clarke (83) demonstrates the cross leg shuffle as he takes the baton from new member L.Lyons.
Top right. M.Harrison (13) demonstrates the walkers change as he hands over to P.Moysey.
Bottom left. Steve Webb (69) milkman to the last gives Pat Lyttle no change.
Centre. Ian Morton (75) provides a fine example of the jumping high level pass with Graham Allerton intercepting.
Bottom right. Colin Pearson (84) uses the jumping low level pass to send Tony Fairclough on his way.
The successful Surrey Road Team, Kevin Clarke, Alister Horton, Paul Richley, Stuart Paton and Gerry Sexton.

photo.caption:

Top right. M.Harrison (13) demonstrates the walkers change as he hands over to P.Moysey.
Bottom left. Steve Webb (69) milkman to the last gives Pat Lyttle no change.

mentions.h: Men and Women - Road Running - Rankings 1997

photos.c: For years Derek Clack has said that in all the time he's been in the club he's not yet had his picture published. Sorry Derek - it's a case of too few photographers required to be in too many places at the right time. However, The Wimbledon Guardian seems to be a little better off in the way of human resource and sent their photographer to snap Derek and Sue after their gruelling hike from John O'Groats to Lands End. The 920 mile walk took our intrepid couple seven weeks but it was well worth it for they raised £1000 for the Tadworth Children's Trust. They got lost for a while at Loch Ness and nearly went over a cliff, got stranded out on the West Highland Way as night fell, suffered from blisters ... makes those training reps up Wool Road seem like a piece of cake!

photos.c: Above: the record low-scoring team in the Surrey 10k Championships: Gabby Collison, 3rd, Helen Maskrey, 1st, and Morag Andrew, 2nd.

Left: Our fastest 1st-Claim 3,000 metre runner from last summer, Gabrielle Collison, turns into Horton Lane with nearly 2 miles to go in the 26.2/Securicor 10k on 7th February. Running strongly, she went on to place 3rd in the Surrey Championship, held in conjunction, giving our team the perfect score of 6 points.

Above: Gabrielle Collison is our "athlete of the moment". In late summer she clocked 9:48 for 3000m and 4:38.6 for 1,500m on the track, respectively our fastest and fourth fastest times ever. She followed this up in the autumn with some great road runs and then two outstanding wins in the Surrey Women's Cross Country League Division One. Gabby has always worked hard in training and races but has only recently discovered that she has been suffering from anaemia. A course of treatment for the disorder has worked wonders and as a result, our already upwardly mobile women's road and cross country section has received another boost.

photos.c: Above: Gabby Collison (4) was our top 800 metre runner in 1991 and was ranked second over 1,500 metres.
Gabby Collison (left) and Jacqui Smiter brave the frozen wastes of Frimley during the Surrey Cross Country Championships.

Left: Gabby Collison (2), Jacinta Moore (6) and Martina Ryan (just visible behind and to the right of 37) are well involved in the initial rush across the playing fields in the Surrey Cross-Country Champs at Frimley.
Left: Belgrave's Number One on Country, Road and Track.

It's been fine Autumn for Gabby Collison.  Coming off the track with a trio of sub-10 minutes 3,000m races and a 16:52.1 5,000m at Crawley in September, she then transferred her attentions to the road.
The Great South Run at Portsmouth saw her unleash a marvellous 57:57 to remove over 2½ minutes from the Club Record for 10 miles and two weeks later her season's best for 10k came down to 35:50 at Basingstoke's Klix '6'.  The AAA and Inter-County 10k Championship was held at Barnsley on November 2nd and representing Surrey she improved again to 35:22 for a superb 8th place in this top class race.  A win at one of her local events at Preston Park came seven days later and was followed on November 16th by 1st place in the Brighton & Hove 10k in 34:46 – just 14 seconds short of her own and Belgrave's best ever performance set in 1995.  Then on to the Victory '5' at Portsmouth where another of her marks from 1995 barely survived as she clocked 27:57 for the 5 mile course.

photos.c: Back Page Photo: One of the most expressive shots of the year. Belgravian Darren Campbell representing Great Britain & Northern Ireland continues the Linford Christie tradition by winning the European Games 100 metres Championship in a record time of 10.04 seconds.
Relaxed and smooth, Darren Campbell eases to an impressive win in the early rounds of the 100 metres at Budapest.
Darren Campbell is interviewed over the public address and explains to the French crowd how the British 4 x 100 metres squad is going to give the Americans big trouble at the Sydney 2000 Olympics.
Bottom right - Darren Campbell celebrated Olympic silver after a brilliant run in the Olympic 200 metres where he became third fastest Briton of all time.

1. One of the most glorious sights in athletics is the start of the Senior Men's National Cross Country Championships. Half a mile into the 2000 race at Stowe School, Buckinghhamshire, and the field is led by Belgrave's Paul Evans with Paul Freary just behind him and to the right. On the left, behind 2516 is Kevin Nash and next but one above 2321 is Rob McHarg. On the right, behind the orange vested .24 is Jason Lobo, making a more conservative start, with Lee Hurst next but one on the left of .24. In the centre, just behind and to the right of the Blackheath vest is Alaster Stewart and next on the right, with only his claret bandana showing is Charles Herrington. That's eight in the top 100 and they spent the next half mile gaining even more forward positions. You might have to take the Editor's word for this one: on the skyline just to the left of the tree can be seen Phil Carstairs' thinning thatch. Will Cockerell has also been picked out in this vicinity by one viewer - but blowed if we can find him now!

Just as some men hate Parliament Hill, others seem to love it. Every year Phil Carstairs turns out for the Southern Cross Country Champs., improves his best position and sees the team edging ever closer to the medals.

Right: An hour before "National" race time. Bill Laws and John Jeffery have driven back to Milton Keynes to pick up Paul Evans whose car has broken down, leaving the rest of the team to pose for the pre-race photo. Front: Darryl Ochse, Will Cockerell, Charles Herrington, Lee Hurst, Rob McHarg.
